q: Funny captions on my dog video, big white text with a black outline like a meme.
a: A graphic with a text layer at the top (and one at the bottom) in a bold font, white with a black stroke (`graphics.set` for the stroke, or a shape behind pinned with `graphics.pin`). Time each caption to the moment, held long enough to read twice; a quick punch-in (Motion Scale) on the funny beat and a sound effect sell the joke.

q: cat video with a slow zoom on its face and dramatic music
a: Keyframe Motion Scale slowly up towards the face (Position keeps it centred), eased in; the music on its own track entering at the zoom's start. A Hold keyframe at the end freezes the framing for the punchline.

q: Same caption style on 20 pet clips for a compilation.
a: Make the caption graphic once and export it as a template with only the text editable (`graphics.template.export`); apply it to each clip (`graphics.template.apply`) and type the new line.

q: Make someone's eyes glow for a supernatural moment.
a: On a node, two small soft ellipse windows on the eyes (`masks.add`), tracked to the face (`masks.track`), with Gain pushed bright and towards the colour you want. For a halo, a copy above with Wonder Glow (Lights & Glows) limited to the eyes by a mask on Opacity. Keyframe it on for the moment; fast head turns need the track checked frame by frame.

q: eyes flash red for one second
a: Windows on the eyes on their own node, tracked; push Gain towards red. To make it last one second, cut the clip around the moment (`sequence.addEdit`) and put that node only on the middle piece, or keyframe an Opacity-masked red glow copy on and off.

q: Glowing eyes but the person blinks and the glow stays.
a: The window keeps glowing over closed lids: keyframe the effect off for the blink frames (cut the clip and drop the node there, or keyframe the glow copy's Opacity to 0 during the blink).

q: Add a lightning flash to my stormy night shot.
a: Brightness flashes: Lumetri on the clip with Exposure keyframed up for 1–2 frames, down, and a smaller second flash (lightning flickers). A thunder sound a moment later on an SFX track. Revolution has no lightning-bolt generator: a bolt comes from overlay footage on Screen.

q: storm scene: lightning flashes plus rain sound plus darker grade
a: Darker, cooler, desaturated grade; Exposure flashes keyframed on a Lumetri effect (or an Adjustment Layer above several clips so all flash together); rain ambience typed Ambience under the scene and thunder hits as SFX.

q: Flash should light up the whole sequence of shots at once.
a: An Adjustment Layer (File ▸ New) above all the shots with Lumetri, Exposure keyframed for each flash: one place to time every flash.

q: Zoom from a world map down to my city, like a travel intro.
a: Revolution has no map or globe generator. Use a large map image (one you're licensed to use): import it, keyframe Motion Scale from small to very large with Position centring your city, eased in and out. A high-resolution image avoids softness at the end; a pin graphic and the city name appear when the zoom lands.

q: animated route line on a map between two cities
a: A line shape layer in a graphic whose Scale X is keyframed from 0 (anchored at the start city) draws a straight route; for a curved route, several short segments or make it elsewhere and import it.

q: Map zoom gets blurry at the end.
a: The image runs out of resolution: use a bigger map, zoom less, or cut to a second, more detailed map image at the end with a dissolve.

q: Old-movie spinning newspaper headline that stops in front of the camera.
a: Make the front page as a graphic or image. Apply 3D Rotate or the Transform effect and keyframe Rotation (several full turns) and Scale from tiny to full over a second, with an ease-out so it lands; add a whoosh. Grade it sepia with grain for period.

q: spinning headline but I also want it tilted in 3D
a: 3D Rotate (Video Effects ▸ Transform) with X / Y Rotation and Perspective gives the tilt; keyframe Z Rotation for the spin and Z Position to fly it in.

q: Several headlines spinning in one after another for a montage.
a: Build the first, save the spin as a preset with keyframes anchored to the In point (`presets.save`), and apply it to each headline clip.

q: Make an old photo come alive with a 3D parallax move.
a: Cut the person out of the photo with a mask (on a copy above, `masks.add`, feathered); keep the full photo below. Keyframe the foreground copy to scale a little more than the background (e.g. 100 → 112 % vs 100 → 104 %) so they separate. Revolution can't fill in the background behind the person: the original under them hides the gap if the move is small.

q: parallax on a landscape photo with foreground, middle and sky layers
a: Three copies stacked, each masked to its layer (foreground, middle, sky), each with its own Scale / Position keyframes (foreground moves most). A comp makes the layers easier to see as a graph (Media In → Mask → Transform → Merge).

q: Parallax photo edges show holes when I move the layers.
a: Moves bigger than the overlap reveal gaps; keep the moves small, scale the background up a little, or paint the gap out in an image editor before importing.

q: Clean up a recorded video call with four people for YouTube.
a: 1. Clean Up Voice on the call audio (`audio.cleanupVoice`) or Voice Isolation for keyboard and room noise. 2. Remove long pauses and filler words from the transcript (`transcript.removePauses`, `transcript.removeFillers`). 3. Punch in on the speaker's tile with Motion Scale / Position when one person talks for a while. 4. Captions from the transcript.

q: call recording, one person is much quieter than others
a: If everyone is on one mixed track, the quiet voice can only be lifted where they talk: Volume keyframes or a clip split with more gain (`clip.audioGain`); Dynamics in Essential Sound evens it out. Separate tracks per person (if the call app records them) are far easier.

q: Show the gallery view but zoom to whoever is talking.
a: No automatic active-speaker switching: cut at each speaker change and punch in on their tile (Motion Scale / Position); the transcript shows where the changes are.

q: A glitchy title for a tech video.
a: The title graphic with the bundled Glitch shader effect (Video Effects ▸ User ▸ Stylize) or RGB Split (Lights & Glows); keyframe them strong for the first few frames, then calm. A Glitch transition into the next shot ties it together. GPU only for the shader.

q: title that flickers in letter by letter with a digital look
a: Fade letters with per-character styles or several text layers, plus a short Glitch shader burst keyframed on each appearance; Posterize Time on the graphic makes the motion steppy.

q: Chromatic aberration on just the title, not the footage.
a: Put the effect (Chromatic Aberration shader or RGB Split) on the title graphic's clip only; effects on a track above don't touch the footage below unless it's an adjustment layer.

q: Add an explosion behind my actor running away.
a: An explosion clip shot on black above the shot with Screen blend (black disappears), placed and scaled behind the actor; mask the actor back in front if the blast covers them (a tracked mask on a copy of the shot above). Camera Shake on the shot for the hit, an Exposure flash keyframed on the frame of the blast, and a boom sound. No particle generator: the fire comes from footage.

q: explosion looks fake, too clean
a: Grade the explosion to the shot's light and contrast, add some of its warm light onto the scene (a soft window with Gain pushed warm, keyframed), match grain, and add shake and a flash on the hit.

q: Debris and smoke after the blast.
a: Stock smoke and debris overlays on black (Screen) or on transparency, layered over the shot and the explosion; no particles or simulation in Revolution.

q: Running score graphic on a sports video that I update as goals happen.
a: A graphic with the team names and score as text layers, saved as a template with the scores editable (`graphics.template.export`). Place a new copy at each goal and change the score (`graphics.template.set` or Essential Graphics ▸ Edit), clips end to end on a top track.

q: scoreboard with a game clock
a: The clock: Metadata & Timecode Burn-in shows the sequence timecode ticking (set its position and size); a real match clock that stops and starts needs separate pieces or keyframed text.

q: Score bug that animates when a goal is scored.
a: In the template, a short Scale bump or colour flash on the score layer at the clip's start (protected in-time, `graphics.setResponsiveTime`), so every new score clip pops when it appears.
